title: Concentration Risk Index for AI Model Ecosystems

original_idea.title: Concentration Risk Index for AI Model Ecosystems
original_idea.problem: Financial regulators use HHI to measure market concentration. No analogous tool exists for AI deployment ecosystems.
original_idea.direction: Define an 'AI Concentration Risk Index' based on output similarity weighted by market deployment share, and compute it for publicly known deployment statistics of major model providers.
original_idea.why_it_matters: A quantitative index would give regulators and researchers a single trackable number to monitor systemic risk from AI monoculture.
original_idea.relevant_context: CEPR economists have explicitly drawn the analogy between AI concentration and financial systemic risk; Sidley Austin (2024) documents ECB concerns about AI monoculture in finance.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: an index for regulators is useful, but the chain from defining an index to improved safety depends on adoption and policy action.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: adapting HHI requires some economic and mathematical background but the formula is well-documented and implementable by CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a defined index formula computed on publicly available deployment data, with a clear numerical output.

title: Semantic Clustering of Safety Refusals: How Many Distinct Refusal Strategies Exist Across the Ecosystem?

original_idea.title: Semantic Clustering of Safety Refusals: How Many Distinct Refusal Strategies Exist Across the Ecosystem?
original_idea.problem: Safety refusals from different models may all sound different while encoding the same underlying strategy, or vice versa -- there is no empirical map of refusal diversity across the AI ecosystem.
original_idea.direction: Collect refusal responses from 15+ models on 500 standardized harmful prompts, cluster them semantically and structurally, and count the effective number of distinct refusal strategies.
original_idea.why_it_matters: A small number of shared refusal strategies means an adversary who breaks one breaks all -- a direct systemic safety risk.
original_idea.relevant_context: AILuminate v1.0 provides a 24K-prompt safety test set that can be used as the probe. Universal transferable attacks show cross-model vulnerability already exists.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: directly demonstrates whether breaking one refusal strategy breaks all models. This is a direct systemic safety risk finding with immediate implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: collecting refusals from 15+ models requires API access and cost, and semantic clustering requires embedding and clustering skills, but these are learnable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: running 15+ models on 500 prompts, collecting outputs, and performing clustering analysis is significant in compute, API cost, and time for 30 hours.

title: Testing the Artificial Hivemind Effect on Structured Safety Reasoning Tasks

original_idea.title: Testing the Artificial Hivemind Effect on Structured Safety Reasoning Tasks
original_idea.problem: The original Artificial Hivemind paper tested open-ended generative tasks. It is unknown whether the same homogeneity effect holds for structured safety reasoning tasks.
original_idea.direction: Use the Infinity-Chat methodology -- pairwise semantic similarity across models -- but replace open-ended queries with a curated set of safety reasoning tasks. Measure whether homogeneity coefficients are higher, lower, or the same.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Safety reasoning tasks are more directly consequential than creative tasks; establishing whether homogeneity carries over is a direct safety research priority.
original_idea.relevant_context: Infinity-Chat benchmark (26K queries, 31K annotations, 70+ models); AILuminate safety hazard categories provide a ready-made task bank.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: directly extends the Artificial Hivemind finding to safety-relevant tasks, which are more consequential. A positive finding has immediate safety implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: replicating the Infinity-Chat methodology with new task types requires understanding the protocol and analysis pipeline, but the original paper provides guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: homogeneity coefficients on safety reasoning tasks compared to original open-ended baseline, with a clear numerical comparison.

title: Artificial Hivemind in Reasoning Models: Do o3, DeepSeek-R1, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet Show Different Homogeneity Profiles?

original_idea.title: Artificial Hivemind in Reasoning Models: Do o3, DeepSeek-R1, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet Show Different Homogeneity Profiles?
original_idea.problem: The Artificial Hivemind paper predates the widespread deployment of explicit reasoning models. These models may show different homogeneity patterns.
original_idea.direction: Replicate the Artificial Hivemind measurement protocol on a subset of Infinity-Chat queries using 5+ reasoning models, comparing their homogeneity coefficients to the original non-reasoning model baseline.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Reasoning models are increasingly deployed for high-stakes decisions; if they are equally or more homogeneous, systemic risk grows as these models replace general-purpose ones.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind covered 70+ models, but reasoning models with explicit CoT (o3, DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet) were not the focus of analysis.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: reasoning models are increasingly deployed for high-stakes decisions. Understanding their homogeneity profile directly informs systemic risk assessment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: replicating the measurement protocol on reasoning models requires API access and understanding the similarity analysis, but is guided by the original methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: homogeneity coefficients for reasoning models compared to the non-reasoning baseline, using a subset of existing queries.

title: Multimodal Homogeneity: Do Vision-Language Models Converge on Image Descriptions?

original_idea.title: Multimodal Homogeneity: Do Vision-Language Models Converge on Image Descriptions?
original_idea.problem: The Artificial Hivemind effect has only been documented for text-only models. It is unknown whether multimodal models show the same convergence on image captioning and visual question answering.
original_idea.direction: Adapt the pairwise similarity methodology to image description tasks: feed the same set of 500+ images to 5+ VLMs and measure inter-model semantic similarity of generated descriptions.
original_idea.why_it_matters: VLMs are deployed in high-stakes visual domains (medical imaging, surveillance, accessibility tools); homogeneous visual interpretation creates correlated failure risk.
original_idea.relevant_context: Chain of Attack (CVPR 2025) shows adversarial transferability across multimodal models; Artificial Hivemind documents the effect in text only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: extending to VLMs is interesting and relevant to high-stakes visual domains, but the safety impact chain is less direct than text-based safety tasks.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: working with multiple VLMs, managing image datasets, and handling multimodal API calls requires more infrastructure and expertise than beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: running 5+ VLMs on 500+ images and computing similarity is substantial in terms of compute, API cost, and data management.

title: Hivemind Effect on Code Generation: Shared Bugs Across AI Coding Assistants

original_idea.title: Hivemind Effect on Code Generation: Shared Bugs Across AI Coding Assistants
original_idea.problem: If multiple AI coding assistants generate structurally similar code for the same specifications, they likely share the same security vulnerabilities and logic errors.
original_idea.direction: Give identical coding prompts to GitHub Copilot, Claude, GPT-4o, and open-source alternatives; measure semantic similarity of generated code and overlap in introduced security vulnerabilities (CWE categories).
original_idea.why_it_matters: Correlated security bugs across all major AI coding tools would represent a systemic risk to software infrastructure at scale.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind methodology applies directly; code similarity and vulnerability overlap can be measured with standard static analysis tools accessible to intro-ML students.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated security bugs across all major AI coding tools is a direct, high-impact safety concern for software supply chains.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: generating code from multiple tools and running static analysis is well-suited for CS students, though coordinating multiple API accesses adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: code similarity and CWE overlap analysis across 4+ coding assistants on a fixed set of prompts.

title: Does Model Size Modulate Homogeneity? Comparing 7B, 13B, 70B, and Frontier Model Homogeneity Profiles

original_idea.title: Does Model Size Modulate Homogeneity? Comparing 7B, 13B, 70B, and Frontier Model Homogeneity Profiles
original_idea.problem: The Artificial Hivemind paper aggregated across model sizes. It is unknown whether smaller or larger models contribute more to inter-model homogeneity.
original_idea.direction: Stratify the existing Infinity-Chat experimental setup by model parameter count and compare intra-size-class vs. cross-size-class homogeneity.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If frontier models are the most homogeneous, the concentration of deployment in this tier amplifies systemic risk; if smaller models are more diverse, this has implications for deployment portfolio design.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind tested 70+ models but did not report size-stratified analysis; the Infinity-Chat benchmark supports this analysis directly.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: understanding the size-homogeneity relationship is informative for deployment strategy, but the direct chain to safety improvement is unclear.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: stratifying existing data by model size and computing similarity metrics is manageable for CS students with data analysis skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: size-stratified homogeneity analysis using existing Infinity-Chat data, with clear intra-class vs. cross-class comparison.

title: Homogeneity Across Prompt Styles: Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models

original_idea.title: Homogeneity Across Prompt Styles: Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models
original_idea.problem: It is unknown whether instruction tuning is the primary driver of inter-model homogeneity or whether homogeneity exists at the base model level.
original_idea.direction: Compare inter-model similarity between base model variants vs. their instruction-tuned counterparts on a matched set of prompts from Infinity-Chat, isolating the contribution of instruction tuning to homogeneity.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Identifying instruction tuning as a driver would point directly at the intervention needed -- more diverse fine-tuning data and procedures.
original_idea.relevant_context: RLHF reduces diversity vs. SFT (ICLR 2024); Artificial Hivemind documents the endpoint but not the mechanism; this design would partially resolve the mechanism question.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: identifying instruction tuning as the driver of homogeneity directly points to the intervention needed, making this actionable research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: comparing base vs. instruction-tuned model variants requires running open-source models in both configurations, which is feasible with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: controlled comparison isolating instruction tuning's contribution to homogeneity on a matched prompt set.

title: Agentic Task Homogeneity: Do Multi-Step AI Agents Converge on Similar Action Sequences?

original_idea.title: Agentic Task Homogeneity: Do Multi-Step AI Agents Converge on Similar Action Sequences?
original_idea.problem: As AI agents execute multi-step tasks autonomously, correlated action choices across different agent systems could produce coordinated failures.
original_idea.direction: Design a set of agentic benchmark tasks and measure whether different agent frameworks take structurally similar action sequences.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Agentic systems operating in shared environments are more likely to produce observable real-world harm from correlated failures than passive text generators.
original_idea.relevant_context: AI Risk Repository (2025) added multi-agent risks as a new subdomain. Artificial Hivemind methodology can be extended to action sequence comparison.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: agentic homogeneity is a concerning direction, but the research is more exploratory than directly addressing a known safety-critical issue.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: setting up multiple agent frameworks (AutoGPT, LangChain, Claude agents) and designing multi-step benchmark tasks requires significant infrastructure and expertise.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: designing agentic benchmarks from scratch and comparing multiple frameworks is open-ended and likely exceeds 30 hours.

title: Cross-Cultural Homogeneity: Does the Hivemind Effect Vary by Language and Cultural Context?

original_idea.title: Cross-Cultural Homogeneity: Does the Hivemind Effect Vary by Language and Cultural Context?
original_idea.problem: Artificial Hivemind was conducted primarily in English. Models trained on multilingual data may show different homogeneity patterns when queried in other languages.
original_idea.direction: Translate a subset of Infinity-Chat queries into 5+ languages with diverse script and cultural traditions, run them through multilingual-capable models, and compare homogeneity across language conditions.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If homogeneity is weaker in non-English contexts, this identifies a protective factor; if stronger, it signals that non-English communities face equal or greater systemic risk.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind paper is English-focused; cultural and linguistic homogeneity in LLMs is an underexplored dimension.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: understanding cross-cultural homogeneity is an interesting equity question, but the chain to direct safety improvement is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: high-quality translation across 5+ languages, multilingual model access, and cross-cultural analysis require expertise beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: covering 5+ languages across multiple models with quality translations is very ambitious for a 30-hour project.

title: Homogeneity Under Distribution Shift: Does Model Diversity Collapse on Out-of-Distribution Prompts?

original_idea.title: Homogeneity Under Distribution Shift: Does Model Diversity Collapse on Out-of-Distribution Prompts?
original_idea.problem: Models may appear diverse on standard benchmarks but converge on similar (often incorrect) responses when given out-of-distribution or adversarially shifted prompts.
original_idea.direction: Apply systematic prompt perturbations (paraphrase, domain shift, unusual formatting) to Infinity-Chat queries and measure whether inter-model similarity increases on OOD variants.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Safety failures often occur at distribution boundaries. If models converge precisely when inputs are novel or adversarial, the safety risk from homogeneity is concentrated at the most dangerous moments.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind methodology; OOD evaluation is standard in ML robustness literature; the combination has not been studied.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if models converge precisely when inputs are novel or adversarial, the safety risk from homogeneity is concentrated at the most dangerous moments. This is a critical finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: applying prompt perturbations and measuring similarity changes is feasible, though designing good OOD perturbations requires some care.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: comparison of homogeneity coefficients on standard vs. OOD-perturbed prompts, with clear numerical metrics.

original_idea.title: Artificial Hivemind on Long-Context Tasks: Does Homogeneity Persist Over Extended Reasoning?
original_idea.problem: The Artificial Hivemind paper focused on short open-ended queries. Long-context tasks may show different homogeneity profiles.
original_idea.direction: Adapt the homogeneity measurement protocol to long-context inputs (5K-100K tokens) such as document summarization, legal contract analysis, and scientific paper review. Compare homogeneity coefficients to short-context baselines.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Long-context models are increasingly deployed for high-stakes analysis tasks. Understanding whether diversity increases or decreases with context length guides deployment strategy.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind (NeurIPS 2025); recent frontier models now support 1M+ token contexts, making this feasible.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: understanding long-context homogeneity is informative for deployment strategy, but the direct safety action from the finding is unclear.

title: Measuring Intra-Model Repetition as a Function of Temperature and Sampling Parameters

original_idea.title: Measuring Intra-Model Repetition as a Function of Temperature and Sampling Parameters
original_idea.problem: Intra-model repetition is partly controlled by sampling temperature, but the relationship between temperature settings, deployment practices, and observed homogeneity is unstudied.
original_idea.direction: Systematically vary temperature, top-p, and top-k settings for 5+ models on a fixed prompt set and measure intra-model repetition rates, finding the practical parameter regimes where homogeneity can be reduced without sacrificing quality.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If simple parameter changes substantially reduce homogeneity, this is an immediately actionable finding for deployers.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind documents intra-model repetition as a core finding; the role of decoding parameters is mentioned but not fully investigated.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: finding actionable parameter changes for deployers is useful, but the safety impact chain is indirect -- it addresses homogeneity, not safety directly.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: varying temperature, top-p, and top-k parameters via API calls and measuring repetition is very accessible for beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: systematic parameter sweep on a fixed prompt set across 5+ models with clear metrics. Well-bounded and completable in 30 hours.

title: Replication of Intra-Model Repetition Across Temporal Sessions

original_idea.title: Replication of Intra-Model Repetition Across Temporal Sessions
original_idea.problem: It is unknown whether intra-model repetition persists across temporal sessions, which would indicate systemic persistence rather than a run-time artifact.
original_idea.direction: Re-run a fixed set of probes from Infinity-Chat on the same model API endpoints at 30-day intervals over 3-6 months and track similarity scores.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Temporal persistence of homogeneity would indicate that the problem is architectural and training-based rather than correctable through inference-time parameters.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind documents intra-model repetition but does not track temporal stability. This directly follows up on finding (a).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: temporal persistence is informative for understanding the root cause, but it doesn't directly improve safety outcomes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: re-running probes at intervals and tracking similarity scores is straightforward and requires only API calls and basic analysis.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: the project requires 3-6 months of data collection at 30-day intervals, far exceeding the 30-hour timeframe constraint.
